mainTopic: Whether a buyer's vessel acquires in the seller's domain, and when movable items are acquired by משיכה versus הגבהה
overview: The amud opens with רבא finishing a ברייתא about goods unloaded into the buyer's house. He uses it to argue that a buyer's vessel standing in the seller's domain does not acquire for him. רב נחמן בר יצחק and then מר בר רב אשי push off that proof, saying the case may have no vessels at all, such as bundles of garlic. רבינא explains that fixing a price matters because it shows a firm decision to sell. He then tries a proof from רב and שמואל, who say 'a person's vessel acquires for him in any place.' רב אשי limits that rule to where the seller said 'go acquire.' Next the גמרא quotes a משנה: movable items are acquired by משיכה. An אמורא limits it: items people usually lift must be acquired by הגבהה, not by pulling. That rule is tested twice. First comes a ברייתא about a stolen purse, which אביי explains as a purse heavy enough to need a rope. Then comes a ברייתא about buying in the seller's domain, which רב נחמן בר יצחק reads as two separate cases.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: unloading into the buyer's house
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes quoting the ברייתא. If the goods were unloaded into the buyer's house, then fixing the price before measuring locks in the sale, but measuring before fixing the price does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he unloaded the goods and brought them into the buyer's house: if he set the price before measuring, neither side can back out. If he measured before setting the price, both sides can still back out.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last part of the ברייתא that רבא is using as his proof. It describes goods unloaded into the buyer's house, and it explains when the sale becomes final.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the goods are inside the buyer's house, the buyer's domain can make the sale take effect. Whether it actually does depends on whether a price was already fixed. If there was no fixed price, either side may still back out. רבא will now draw an inference from this case.

keyTerms.meaning: he unloaded them (took the goods off the donkeys)
he fixed (set) the price
he measured the goods
to back out of the deal

phrases.english: If he unloaded them and brought them into his house;
phrases.notes: 'His house' means the buyer's house. The goods are still in the seller's containers, which is the whole point of רבא's proof.

phrases.english: if he fixed the price before he measured,
neither of them can back out;
if he measured before he fixed the price,
both of them can back out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא that רבא began quoting before this section.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a buyer's vessel in the seller's domain acquires for the buyer.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about goods unloaded into the buyer's house.

steps.title: רבא's inference: vessels don't override the domain
steps.stepSummary: The seller's vessel in the buyer's domain does not keep the goods for the seller. So the buyer's vessel in the seller's domain should not acquire for the buyer either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the seller's vessels in the buyer's domain don't keep ownership for the seller, the buyer's vessels in the seller's domain also don't acquire for the buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא draws his conclusion from the ברייתא. In it, the goods sat in the seller's containers inside the buyer's house, and the buyer still acquired them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the domain beat the vessel: the buyer's house won out over the seller's containers. רבא turns this around. In the opposite case, the seller's domain should also beat the buyer's vessel, so the buyer would not acquire.

keyTerms.meaning: a vessel or container, which can acquire for its owner
domain (whose property it is in)
the buyer
the seller

phrases.aramaic: וּמִדְּכִלְיוֹ דְמוֹכֵר בִּרְשׁוּת לוֹקֵחַ – לֹא קָנָה,
phrases.english: And since the seller's vessel in the buyer's domain does not acquire,
phrases.notes: He means it doesn't hold on to the goods for the seller, so the buyer gets them.

phrases.english: the buyer's vessel too,
in the seller's domain, does not acquire!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדְּכִלְיוֹ דְמוֹכֵר בִּרְשׁוּת לוֹקֵחַ לֹא קָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.raayaObject: A buyer's vessel in the seller's domain does not acquire.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The reverse case in the ברייתא: the seller's vessel inside the buyer's house.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: the goods were poured out
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק rejects the proof. He says the ברייתא is talking about a case where the goods were emptied out of the seller's vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: it is talking about where he poured them out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק pushes back on רבא's proof. He reads the ברייתא as a case where the goods were dumped onto the buyer's floor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the goods were poured out, the seller's vessels are no longer involved. Then the ברייתא teaches nothing about vessels against domains, and רבא's inference falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: he poured them out (emptied the containers)

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Where he poured them out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק בְּשֶׁשְּׁפָכָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof by reading the ברייתא as a different case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not prove the opposite.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may involve no vessels at all, since the goods were poured out.

steps.title: רבא objects: the ברייתא says 'unloaded,' not 'poured'
steps.stepSummary: רבא gets upset and points to the exact word in the ברייתא. It says 'unloaded,' which means the goods stayed in their containers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא got angry: does it say 'poured them out'? It says 'unloaded them'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the rejection, using the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Unloading' means taking the containers off the donkey, goods and all. 'Pouring' would be a different word. So רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading doesn't fit the text.

keyTerms.meaning: he became angry or upset
does it teach...? (a sharp question pointing to the wording)

phrases.english: Rava became angry:
Does it teach 'he poured them out'?!
It teaches 'he unloaded them'!

steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading 'where he poured them out.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording 'פירקן' means unloading the containers whole, not emptying them.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי: bundles of garlic
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי rejects רבא's proof in a new way. The ברייתא is about bundles of garlic, which are unloaded with no containers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, מר בר רב אשי said: it is talking about bundles of garlic.
steps.whatsHappening: Since 'poured out' doesn't fit the wording, the גמרא offers a different reading that still knocks down רבא's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bundles of garlic come off the donkey with no vessels at all. So the word 'unloaded' fits perfectly, and still no seller's vessels are involved. רבא's inference about vessels and domains is still not proven.

keyTerms.meaning: bundles of garlic tied together

steps.confusionAlert: This does not prove that the buyer's vessel DOES acquire in the seller's domain. It only shows that רבא's proof doesn't work, so the question stays open.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rather, Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
With bundles of garlic.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי בִּמְתַאכְּלֵי דְתוּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading of step 3 with one that fits the word 'unloaded.'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may involve goods that have no containers, so it says nothing about vessels.

steps.title: Why should fixing the price matter?
steps.stepSummary: הונא בריה דמר זוטרא asks רבינא a question. If unloading into the buyer's house is what acquires, why does it matter whether a price was fixed?
steps.simpleTranslation: הונא son of מר זוטרא said to רבינא: since it says 'he unloaded them,' what difference does it make whether he fixed the price or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to the ברייתא itself and questions its logic. This sets up רבינא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unloading the goods into the buyer's domain should be a complete act of acquisition. So the price question seems irrelevant, yet the ברייתא makes the whole outcome depend on it.

keyTerms.meaning: since, after all
what difference does it make to me

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּמָר זוּטְרָא לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Huna son of Mar Zutra said to Ravina:
After all, it teaches 'he unloaded them';

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי פָּסַק וּמָה לִי לֹא פָּסַק?
phrases.english: what difference is it to me whether he fixed the price or did not fix it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי פֵּירְקָן קָתָנֵי מָה לִי פָּסַק וּמָה לִי לֹא פָּסַק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the proof debate and questions the ברייתא's own rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's distinction between fixing the price before or after measuring.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the act of acquisition (unloading into the buyer's house) is done, the price should not matter.

steps.title: A fixed price shows a firm decision
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that fixing the price shows the seller has truly decided to sell. Without a fixed price there is no firm decision, so the act of acquisition doesn't take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: if he fixed the price, he has made up his mind. If he didn't fix it, he hasn't made up his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא explains why the price matters even after the goods were unloaded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An act of acquisition only works when both sides really intend to complete the deal. Without a set price, nobody has fully committed. So the unloading alone does not seal the sale.

keyTerms.meaning: his mind is settled, he has firmly decided

steps.whatToRemember: Acquisition needs both an act (like unloading into the buyer's domain) and a firm decision (like a fixed price).

phrases.english: He said to him:
If he fixed the price, his mind is settled;
if he did not fix it, his mind is not settled.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּסַק סָמְכָא דַּעְתֵּיהּ לֹא פָּסַק לָא סָמְכָא דַּעְתֵּיהּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the reason behind the rule (intent, called גמירות דעת).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The physical act of unloading alone should finish the sale.
steps.terutzMaskana: The act works only together with a firm decision, which a fixed price shows.

steps.title: רבינא's proof from רב and שמואל: 'in any place'
steps.stepSummary: רבינא brings a teaching of רב and שמואל: a person's vessel acquires for him in any place. He suggests that 'any place' includes even the seller's domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: come and hear, since רב and שמואל both say: a person's vessel acquires for him in any place. What does that come to include? Doesn't it include the seller's domain?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the main open question and tries a new proof, this time in the other direction: that the buyer's vessel does acquire in the seller's domain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'in any place' sound like they add something unusual. The most likely new case is a vessel sitting in the seller's own domain. If so, the buyer's vessel would acquire even there.

keyTerms.meaning: both of them
in any place
what does this come to include?

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּרַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rav and Shmuel both say:

phrases.aramaic: כִּלְיוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם קוֹנֶה לוֹ בְּכׇל מָקוֹם.
phrases.english: A person's vessel acquires for him in any place.
What does this come to include?
Does it not come to include the seller's domain?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע דְּרַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the main question about the buyer's vessel in the seller's domain.
steps.raayaObject: A buyer's vessel acquires even in the seller's domain.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב and שמואל: 'a person's vessel acquires for him in any place.'

steps.title: רב אשי: only where the seller said 'Go acquire'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי pushes off the proof. רב and שמואל are talking about a case where the seller told the buyer, 'Go acquire.'
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is where he told him: go acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי limits רב and שמואל's rule to a special case, so it doesn't prove the general question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the seller says 'go acquire,' he has given the buyer permission to use his space for the buyer's vessel. Without that permission, we still don't know whether the buyer's vessel acquires in the seller's domain.

keyTerms.meaning: there (in that case)
go and acquire

steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs were pushed off. רבא's ברייתא may be about garlic bundles, and רב and שמואל may be about where the seller said 'go acquire.' The question of the buyer's vessel in the seller's domain is still open.

phrases.english: There, it is where he said to him: Go acquire.
phrases.notes: The 'he' who speaks is the seller, giving the buyer permission.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits רב and שמואל's rule to a special case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'In any place' may refer only to where the seller explicitly allowed the buyer to acquire.

steps.title: The משנה on how land and movable items are acquired
steps.stepSummary: A משנה from elsewhere: land is acquired by money, a document or חזקה, and movable items only by משיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: property that has a guarantee (land) is acquired by money, a document, or taking possession. Property without a guarantee (movable items) is acquired only by pulling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a משנה about the ways property is acquired. This sets up the next step, which limits one part of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of property. Land (נכסים שיש להן אחריות) has three ways to be acquired. Movable items (נכסים שאין להן אחריות) have only one way here: משיכה, pulling the item toward yourself.

keyTerms.meaning: Property with a guarantee: land
Property without a guarantee: movable items
Acquiring land by acting as the owner, such as working it
Acquiring a movable item by pulling it toward yourself

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: "There" means a משנה in a different tractate, קידושין 26a.

phrases.english: Property that has a guarantee
phrases.notes: This means land. A creditor can collect from it, so it works like a guarantee for loans.

phrases.english: is acquired by money, by a document, and by taking possession;
and property that has no guarantee
is acquired only by pulling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about how movable items are acquired. It links back to the earlier discussion of קנין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Land is acquired by כסף, שטר or חזקה. Movable items are acquired only by משיכה.

steps.title: Items usually lifted need lifting, not pulling
steps.stepSummary: An אמורא limits the משנה: משיכה works only for items that are not usually lifted. Items people normally lift must be acquired by הגבהה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In סורא they taught this in the name of רב חסדא. In פומבדיתא they taught it in the name of רב כהנא, and some say in the name of רבא: the משנה only meant items that are not usually lifted. Items that are usually lifted are acquired by lifting, yes, but not by pulling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that narrows the משנה. Pulling works only for items too big or awkward to lift. Liftable items need lifting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said movable items are acquired "only by pulling." This teaching says that is not the whole picture. The right act depends on how the item is normally handled. For a liftable item, pulling it is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught it
A teaching or halachic statement
They only taught this about..., a phrase that limits a rule
Acquiring an item by lifting it

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the rule that the rest of the section tests. Liftable items cannot be acquired by משיכה.

phrases.english: In Sura they taught this teaching
in the name of Rav Chisda;

phrases.aramaic: בְּפוּמְבְּדִיתָא מַתְנוּ לַהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא,
phrases.english: in Pumbedita they taught it in the name of Rav Kahana,
and some say in the name of Rava:
They taught this only about items
that are not usually lifted,
but items that are usually lifted,
by lifting, yes; by pulling, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵין דַּרְכָּן לְהַגְבִּיהַּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the משנה's rule about משיכה to items that are not usually lifted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Items that are usually lifted are acquired only by הגבהה, not by משיכה.

steps.title: The ברייתא of the stolen purse on שבת
steps.stepSummary: While אביי teaches the rule, רב אדא בר מתנה brings a ברייתא about a thief who steals a purse on שבת, once by lifting it and once by dragging it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי sat and taught this rule. רב אדא בר מתנה challenged him from a ברייתא: One who steals a purse on שבת must pay, because he already became liable for theft before he broke שבת. If he dragged it out, he is exempt, because the שבת violation and the theft happen at the same moment.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר מתנה quotes a ברייתא to challenge the rule from step 11. Here he only quotes the source. His actual attack comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, if one act brings both the death penalty for חילול שבת and a duty to pay, the person gets only the heavier punishment and does not pay. In the first case the thief lifted the purse inside the house, so the theft was complete before he carried it out, and he must pay. In the dragging case he acquires the purse only as it leaves the house, which is exactly when שבת is broken, so he is exempt from paying.

keyTerms.meaning: One who steals a purse
Dragging it along and going out
Happen at the same moment

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read פטור as "the thief did nothing wrong." He is exempt from paying only because he gets the heavier punishment for breaking שבת.

phrases.english: Abaye sat and was saying this teaching;

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Masna raised an objection to Abaye:
One who steals a purse on Shabbat is liable,
phrases.notes: "Liable" here means he must pay for the theft.

phrases.english: because he already became liable for theft
before he came to the Shabbat prohibition.

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה מְגָרֵר וְיוֹצֵא מְגָרֵר וְיוֹצֵא – פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: If he was dragging it out, dragging it out, he is exempt,
phrases.notes: The words are doubled to show he never lifted it. He dragged it the whole way out.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֲרֵי אִיסּוּר שַׁבָּת וּגְנֵיבָה בָּאִין כְּאֶחָד.
phrases.english: since the Shabbat prohibition and the theft come at the same time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה לְאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict the rule in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule in step 11 that items usually lifted are not acquired by משיכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, the thief who only drags a purse still acquires it, since theft happens as it leaves the house. The full attack is spelled out in step 13.

steps.title: A purse is liftable, yet it is acquired by pulling
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מתנה spells out his challenge: a purse is a liftable item, yet the ברייתא shows it is acquired by dragging.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a purse is an item that is lifted, and even so it is acquired by pulling!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר מתנה states his attack clearly. The ברייתא contradicts the rule that liftable items cannot be acquired by pulling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the dragging case, the theft happens at the moment the purse leaves the house, so the thief acquired it by pulling. A purse is normally lifted. So the ברייתא seems to say liftable items can be acquired by משיכה, against the teaching in step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, used to point out a contradiction
An item that is normally lifted
And even so

phrases.english: But a purse is an item that is lifted,
and even so it is acquired by pulling!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the contradiction out of the ברייתא quoted in step 12.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A purse is liftable, yet the dragging thief acquires it. So liftable items can be acquired by משיכה.

steps.title: אביי answers: with a rope
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the ברייתא is talking about pulling with a rope.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: with a rope.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a very short answer. The ברייתא is about a rope.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי is trying to make the ברייתא a special case so it does not clash with the rule. His answer is so short that it can be misunderstood. The next step shows רב אדא בר מתנה taking it the wrong way.

keyTerms.meaning: A rope

phrases.english: He said to him: With a rope.
phrases.notes: This is אביי speaking. The ברייתא is about a purse pulled with a rope.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by making the ברייתא a rope case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making the ברייתא a special case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about an ordinary liftable purse that was dragged.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא involves a rope. Its exact meaning is clarified in step 16.

steps.title: Even with a rope, it is still pulling
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מתנה replies that a rope does not help: his question already covers a purse pulled by a rope.
steps.simpleTranslation: I too am saying my question about pulling with a rope!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר מתנה pushes back. He took אביי to mean the thief just happened to use a rope, and that is still pulling a liftable item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the purse is small and the thief simply chose to tug it with a rope, the act is still משיכה of a liftable item. So the contradiction remains.

keyTerms.meaning: I too
Am I saying

phrases.english: I too am saying it about a rope!
phrases.notes: This is רב אדא בר מתנה answering back. Pulling with a rope is still pulling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's answer as he understood it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Dragging a liftable purse with a rope is still משיכה of a liftable item, so the contradiction stands.

steps.title: A purse so heavy it needs a rope
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that he meant a purse that needs a rope, one too heavy to lift. Such an item is acquired by משיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I mean an item that needs a rope.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי clears up his answer. He meant a purse so heavy that it can only be moved with a rope.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Such a purse is not a "liftable item" at all. It falls under the משנה's normal rule that items not usually lifted are acquired by משיכה. So the ברייתא fits the teaching in step 11 after all.

keyTerms.meaning: An item that needs

steps.whatToRemember: Whether משיכה or הגבהה is the right act depends on how the item is normally handled. A purse heavy enough to need a rope is acquired by pulling. A normal purse needs lifting.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps the rule from step 11 standing: liftable items need הגבהה.

phrases.english: He said to him: With an item that needs a rope.
phrases.notes: אביי means a purse too heavy to lift, so it can only be moved by pulling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the answer in step 14 and resolves the challenge in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the case: the item is not liftable
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rope was used by chance on an ordinary liftable purse.
steps.terutzMaskana: The purse is too heavy to lift and needs a rope, so משיכה is the proper act and the rule stands.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Items that are usually lifted are acquired only by הגבהה. Items too heavy to lift are acquired by משיכה.

steps.title: A new ברייתא about buying in the seller's domain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: in the seller's domain, the buyer acquires only once he lifts the item or takes it out of the seller's domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If the item is in the seller's domain, the buyer does not acquire it until he lifts it, or until he takes it out of the seller's domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to challenge the rule that a liftable item is acquired only by lifting. This step quotes the source, and the next step will spell out the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives two ways to acquire in the seller's domain: lifting it, or taking it out of his domain. Taking it out can be done by pulling. That second option is what will cause trouble for the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The seller's domain, meaning his property
That he lifts it, the act of הַגְבָּהָה
That he takes it out of his domain

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: בִּרְשׁוּת מוֹכֵר – לֹא קָנָה עַד שֶׁיַּגְבִּיהֶנָּה,
phrases.english: In the seller's domain, he does not acquire it until he lifts it,
or until he takes it out of his domain.
phrases.notes: 'His domain' means the seller's property. Taking it out can be done by pulling it, which is why the גמרא asks a question next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי settled the purse challenge, the גמרא brings a new ברייתא to challenge the same rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that an item normally lifted is acquired only by הַגְבָּהָה, not by מְשִׁיכָה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists two ways to acquire, lifting or removing (pulling), and seems to apply both to the same item.

steps.title: The inference: a liftable item can be acquired either way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the ברייתא as saying that a liftable item may be acquired by lifting or by pulling, whichever the buyer chooses.
steps.simpleTranslation: Evidently, an item that is normally lifted can be acquired by lifting if he wants, and by pulling if he wants!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the challenge from the ברייתא. It reads the word 'or' as a free choice for the same item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא is talking about one kind of item, then a liftable item could also be acquired by מְשִׁיכָה. That directly goes against the rule that liftable items need הַגְבָּהָה.

keyTerms.meaning: Evidently, so we see: introduces what the גמרא learns from a source
An item that is normally lifted
If he wants
Pulling: acquiring an item by drawing it toward oneself

phrases.english: Evidently, an item that is normally lifted:
if he wants, he acquires it by lifting,
and if he wants, he acquires it by pulling!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the problem out of the ברייתא quoted in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a liftable item is acquired only by lifting.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reading 'or' as a choice for one item means a liftable item could also be acquired by pulling, which goes against the rule.

steps.title: The ברייתא is talking about two different kinds of items
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the ברייתא covers two separate cases: liftable items by lifting, and pulled items by pulling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The ברייתא is teaching two separate cases. An item that is normally lifted is acquired by lifting. An item that is normally pulled is acquired by pulling.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the challenge. He says the 'or' in the ברייתא does not mean a choice. Each option belongs to a different kind of item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not let the buyer choose. Lifting goes with liftable items, and taking it out (pulling) goes with heavy items that are pulled. So the rule stands: a liftable item still needs הַגְבָּהָה.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches separate cases: each part of the list applies to a different situation
An item that is normally pulled, not lifted

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's 'lift it, or take it out' is two separate cases, not a choice. Liftable items are acquired by הַגְבָּהָה, and items that get pulled are acquired by מְשִׁיכָה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'or' in the ברייתא as 'whichever you like.' Here it means 'this way for one kind of item, that way for the other kind.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer protects the rule that each kind of item has its own way of being acquired, and it fits with אביי's answer about the heavy purse in step 16.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
It teaches separate cases:
an item that is normally lifted is acquired by lifting;
an item that is normally pulled is acquired by pulling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in steps 17 and 18 by reading the ברייתא differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the source: the list in the ברייתא is split into separate cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא gives the buyer a free choice of lifting or pulling for the same liftable item.
steps.terutzMaskana: Lifting is for liftable items and pulling is for items that get pulled; the rule that liftable items need הַגְבָּהָה stands.
